note: Colour key of Goad (Canada) and Sanborn (US) fire insurance plans c. 1885-1920, as the printed key words it: the wash inside a footprint says the construction material. Applied by fim_blocks.py --legend. Each material names its colour with a word ('yellow', 'pink', 'red', 'blue', 'green', 'grey', 'brown' — also German rot/gelb/blau/gruen/grau and French rouge/jaune/bleu/vert/gris), which the script turns into a broad hue band, so a key transcribed from a text-only legend ('red brick, grey stone') works and scans of different colour balance are tolerated. A key calibrated from a sheet's own reference fills may give exact 'hue_deg': [lo, hi] instead (degrees, HSV 0-360, may wrap). 'grey' means darker than the paper with little chroma. Check against the sheet's printed key; copy this file per edition when the key differs. Vienna's Generalstadtplan has no colour: do not pass a legend there.
source: Goad plan key (frame = yellow, brick = pink/red, stone/concrete = blue, special/fireproof = green). Sanborn adds adobe = grey: add {"name": "adobe", "colour": "grey"} for a Sanborn edition — 'grey' fires on any outline darker than the paper (hatched sheds, stains), so only with a key that has it.
untinted: not a building (open lot, yard or court)
